big_ideas.title: Offense creates an advantage and keeps it; defense denies it and recovers
big_ideas.text: Every possession is a fight over advantage — a step, a numbers edge, a mismatch. Good offense creates one and passes it on until it becomes a good shot; good defense stops the first one and rotates to cancel the next.

big_ideas.title: Space and time are the resources
big_ideas.text: Spacing sets how far each helper must travel; the clock sets how long anyone has. Reads are judgments about distance and time — who is a step late, who has to help, how many seconds are left.

big_ideas.title: The possession is the unit
big_ideas.text: Teams get about the same number of possessions, so points per possession, not points, measures play. Four things decide a possession — shooting, turnovers, rebounding, free throws.

big_ideas.title: Decisions are expected-value bets
big_ideas.text: A shot, a foul, a timeout or a coverage is a bet with a probability and a payoff. The right choice maximises expected points, or win probability late, given the players actually on the floor.

big_ideas.title: The rules shape the strategy
big_ideas.text: Shot clock, team-foul limits, timeout and throw-in rules differ by level (FIBA, NCAA, NFHS), and late-game strategy changes with them. Knowing the rule is part of knowing the play.

big_ideas.title: Decision-makers are developed, not drilled
big_ideas.text: Game IQ grows from representative reps — reading live defenders under time pressure — sequenced by mastery, with competition earning a larger share as players advance.

practices.title: Read the floor
practices.text: Identify the defense, coverage, matchup, where the advantage is and who is the help — from a described possession, a diagram or film.

practices.title: Decide
practices.text: Choose the action (shoot, pass, drive, cut; which coverage; foul or defend) and who it goes to, and say why it beats the alternatives.

practices.title: Apply the rules
practices.text: State the rule for the level being played and what it allows or forbids in the situation — clock, fouls, timeouts, violations, throw-ins.

practices.title: Compute
practices.text: Calculate possessions, efficiency, shooting percentages, expected value and clock math, with the right formula variant and units (per possession, per 100, per shot).

practices.title: Evaluate with context
practices.text: Judge a number or a clip in context — sample size, opponent, role, selection bias, league and era — before drawing a conclusion.

practices.title: Teach and design
practices.text: Turn a principle into a scouting key, a cue, a drill or a practice plan that transfers to games.

los.do: Identify spacing errors in a described or diagrammed half-court set (two players in one help zone, empty corner, crowded lane) and name the fix.
ek: Spacing sets help distance; teaching starts at ~12 ft apart (a lane width) and widens to 15–18 ft and the three-point line as range grows.
A filled corner forces the low helper to choose between the rim and a corner three.

los.do: Given a 5-out, 4-out-1-in or 3-out-2-in alignment and a drive, choose which defender must help and which offensive player is left open.
ek: The nearest helper to the drive's path helps; whoever he left, and the rotation behind him, is the open man.

los.do: Choose the correct spacing move for each off-ball player on a drive — fill, lift, drift, or dive.
ek: Baseline drive: corner lifts to the wing or drifts behind; middle drive: wings drift to the corner, opposite shooters stay one pass away, the big dunker-spots.

los.do: Name the ways an offense creates an advantage (ball screen, post touch, isolation, off-ball screen, transition, offensive rebound) and pick which fits a given personnel group.
ek: Advantage = a defender out of position or a numbers edge; it is created on-ball, off-ball or in the open floor.

los.do: Given a described catch, choose the triple-threat read: shoot if the closeout is late, drive the high foot if the defender is close, pass if help has arrived.
ek: The defender's distance and feet decide: space ⇒ shot, momentum toward you ⇒ drive past it, help shown ⇒ move it.

los.do: Recognise a mismatch in a described lineup (size, speed, a poor defender) and choose how to attack it — post, isolate, or force it into the action.
ek: Attack the mismatch quickly, before the defense scrambles back; involve the weak defender as screener or screened.

topics.title: Keeping the advantage — the advantage chain

los.do: Given a described drive-and-kick sequence, choose the next action for the receiver (shoot, attack the closeout, swing, or extra pass).
ek: Decide on the catch (~0.5 s): an advantage held too long dies as the defense recovers.
The extra pass beats a two-on-one closeout; driving a hard closeout beats a scrambled rotation.

los.do: Distinguish a good shot from a quick shot in a described possession by naming the advantage it came from.
ek: A good shot is an open, in-range attempt from a created advantage; a contested early shot with no advantage wastes the possession.

usab-pdc: Introductory: move to meet the pass

los.do: Given how a defender plays an off-ball screen (trails, goes under, cheats over, top-locks), choose the cut: curl, pop/fade, flare, or backdoor.
ek: Trail ⇒ curl; under or sagging ⇒ pop or fade; top-locked or overplayed ⇒ backdoor; defender shoots the gap ⇒ flare or re-screen.

los.do: Choose when to backdoor, basket-cut or relocate when a defender denies or turns his head.
ek: Denial or ball-watching opens the backdoor; a cut must create a passing lane, not fill one already used.

los.do: Read a described post-entry: choose the entry angle and the post player's read against a double from the top, the baseline or no double.
ek: Enter from the wing at a 45° angle; a double from the top leaves the passer; from the baseline it leaves the opposite block or corner.

los.do: Assign transition lanes and roles (ball, wings sprinting to corners, rim-runner, trailer) for a given rebound or turnover.
ek: Wide lanes stretch the retreat; the rim-runner forces the deepest defender to pick him up; the trailer arrives for a late three or a drag screen.

los.do: Given a 2-on-1, 3-on-2 or 4-on-3 break, choose who shoots or receives the pass.
ek: Make the last defender commit before passing; in a 3-on-2 the first pass usually goes to the wing the top defender didn't take.

los.do: Decide whether to push for an early-offense shot or flow into half-court, given numbers, score and clock.
ek: Push when numbers or mismatches exist before the defense sets; a leading team late may flow into half-court to burn clock.

los.do: Identify the ball-screen type (high, side, drag, step-up, spain, pick-and-pop) and its spacing in a described possession.
ek: Screen angle and location decide which way the ball goes and which helpers are involved.

los.do: Choose the ball-handler's set-up: reject, use, or re-screen, given how the on-ball defender is positioned.
ek: A defender jumping to take away the screen opens the reject; the ball-handler sets up his man before using the screen, shoulder to hip.

los.do: Given a described drop coverage, choose the read: pull-up, floater in the pocket, pop, or lob over a big who is too high.
ek: Drop concedes the pull-up and the pick-and-pop three; a deep drop takes away the roll.

los.do: Given a hedge/show or a blitz, choose the read: escape dribble, pass to the short roll, or skip to the open shooter.
ek: Two on the ball means 4-on-3 behind it; the short-roller is the decision-maker in that 4-on-3.

los.do: Given a switch, choose how to attack: slip before the switch, post the smaller defender, or isolate against the big.
ek: Switching gives up mismatches; slipping punishes an early switch.

los.do: Given ice/blue or weak coverage, choose the counter: reject, pop, or attack downhill to the weak hand.
ek: Ice forces the ball sideline and concedes the pop and long two; rejecting beats a defense that pre-rotates for the screen.

los.do: Given which defender tags the roller, choose the pass: lob, pocket, kick to the tagger's man, or skip to the opposite corner.
ek: If the tag comes from the corner, the corner is open; if it comes from the wing, the skip or the lift is.

los.do: Choose the screener's action — roll, short-roll, pop, slip or ghost — given his skills and the coverage.
ek: Roll vs level/hedge, pop vs drop, slip vs switch or hard hedge, short-roll vs blitz.

los.do: Place each defender correctly given where the ball is — on-ball, one pass away (deny or gap), two passes away (help side).
ek: Ball–you–man: see both; one pass away up the line, two passes away on the line (in the paint), nail help on middle drives.
On-ball: between the man and the basket, about an arm's length, eyes on the waist.

los.do: Choose the direction to force the ball (baseline, middle, weak hand) for a given scheme and scouting report, and justify it.
ek: Forcing baseline needs a low helper waiting; forcing middle relies on bodies in the gaps. Either way, take away the strength.

los.do: Given a described drive or post touch, name who helps, who rotates to the helper's man, and who is left (the X-out or sink-and-fill).
ek: Help comes from the closest gap; rotation goes toward the basket first; the last defender splits two shooters.

los.do: Identify the low man on a described possession and his job when the ball is driven or a roller dives.
ek: Low man = deepest weak-side defender; he protects the rim or tags the roller, and the help behind him zones the two weak-side shooters.

los.do: Choose whether to stunt, dig or fully help on a drive given the driver and the shooter being left.
ek: Stunt and recover vs a non-shooter's teammate; never fully help off an elite shooter one pass away.

los.do: Choose the closeout type (high-hands shot contest, short closeout to take away the drive, run-by) for a described shooter and game situation.
ek: Sprint, then chop the last steps with hands high; close out short on a driver, high on a shooter; late in the game vs a must-make three, run him off the line.

los.do: Assign box-out responsibilities on a described shot, including the shooter and the weak side, where misses go long.
ek: Hit first, then pursue; long shots bounce long, often to the weak side.

los.do: Given a described live-ball turnover or long rebound, choose the transition defense priorities in order: stop the ball, protect the rim, find shooters, match up.
ek: First back takes the rim, the next stops the ball; matching up comes after the paint and the ball are safe.

los.do: Identify the coverage (drop, deep drop, at the level, hedge/show, blitz, ice, weak, switch) from a described position of the screener's defender and the on-ball defender.
ek: Drop: big several feet below the screen; level: at the screen; hedge: above it, then retreats; blitz: above and stays to trap; ice: ball forced sideline, big sitting below; switch: assignments trade.

los.do: State what each coverage takes away and what it concedes.
ek: Drop concedes pull-ups and pops; hedge/blitz concede the short roll and 4-on-3; switch concedes mismatches; ice concedes the pop and long two.

los.do: Given a described ball-handler, screener and your two defenders, choose the coverage and justify it (an auto-checked pick).
ek: Non-shooting ball-handler ⇒ go under / drop; elite shooter ⇒ level, hedge or blitz; non-shooting screener ⇒ ice or drop is cheap; like-sized pair ⇒ switch.
Mobile bigs can hedge and recover; slow bigs can't.

los.do: Choose the over/under/through route for the on-ball defender given the ball-handler's shooting range.
ek: Under a non-shooter, over a shooter; going under a pull-up shooter concedes the three.

los.do: Assign the weak-side help (tagger, low man, X-out) behind a given coverage.
ek: Every coverage that sends two to the ball needs a tag on the roller and a rotation to the tagger's man.

los.do: Identify a zone (2-3, 3-2, 1-3-1, matchup) from a described alignment and response to the first pass.
ek: A zone guards areas, a man defense follows cutters; a matchup zone looks like man until a cutter crosses zones.

los.do: Choose man or a zone for a described opponent and justify it with their shooting, size and depth.
ek: Zones protect foul trouble and size mismatches and concede threes and offensive rebounds; man suits good individual defenders against motion teams.

los.do: Name the weak spots of each standard zone.
ek: 2-3: high post, short corner, skip to corners; 1-3-1: corners and baseline; 3-2: the low blocks.

los.do: Given a described zone and ball position, choose the attack: gap dribble, high-post entry, short-corner feed, skip pass, or overload.
ek: Make two defenders guard one; zones shift on the pass, so skips and quick ball reversal beat them.
Line up in the gaps (odd front vs even, even front vs odd).

los.do: Identify a press (2-2-1, 1-2-1-1, 1-3-1) and its trap locations from a description.
ek: Presses trap near the sideline and the half-court corners, using the line as an extra defender.

los.do: Given a described trap, choose the outlet: middle, reversal, or the long pass over the top.
ek: Don't dribble into the corner trap; the middle and the ball-side flash beat it; the trap leaves someone open behind it.

los.do: Given the game clock, shot clock length and score, compute whether a 2-for-1 is available and when to shoot.
ek: Shoot when game clock ≈ shot clock + 6–10 s: the opponent can't run out the clock, and you still get the last possession.

los.do: Given score, game clock and shot clock, decide whether the leading team can run the clock out, and when the trailing team must foul.
ek: If the game clock is below the shot clock, the leader with the ball can drain it unless fouled; trailing by more than one possession late means foul to stop the clock.

los.do: Choose when to start the attack for a last shot of a quarter or game (hold for one, leave time for a rebound).
ek: Start the action at ~8–6 s so a miss leaves no time for the opponent but a tip remains possible.

los.do: Given a lead of 3, seconds left and the opponent's shooters, decide whether to foul or defend, citing the evidence.
ek: kenpom's college sample: defend ≈ 93.5% vs foul ≈ 92.0% wins, noisy and selection-biased. Fouling is worth it mainly against several good shooters and with confidence in the defensive rebound.
A foul in the act of a three, or a missed FT the trailing team rebounds, is the main risk.

los.do: Trailing by 2 with one possession left, compute the win probability of going for 3 vs going for 2 and overtime, and choose.
ek: P(win | go for 3) = P(make 3); P(win | go for 2) = P(make 2) × P(win OT) — OT is roughly a coin flip unless one side is clearly better.

los.do: Trailing late, choose whom to foul and compute the expected points conceded given the bonus rule for the level.
ek: Two-shot foul ⇒ expected points = 2 × FT%; under a one-and-one ⇒ p + p² (NCAA men's 7th–9th foul).
NFHS: two shots from the 5th team foul in a quarter; FIBA: two shots after 4 team fouls in a quarter; NCAA women: two from the 5th per quarter.

los.do: Choose whether to use a foul to give when leading late, given the opponent's team fouls and time left.
ek: Below the bonus, a non-shooting foul costs only a throw-in and seconds, and breaks up a set play.

los.do: Decide whether to call a timeout or play on after a defensive rebound or made basket late, given timeouts left, the league rule and the defense's state.
ek: Calling a timeout lets a scrambled defense set; FIBA's last-2-minutes option to throw in from the frontcourt throw-in line can make it worth it.

los.do: Apply the timeout allotment and restrictions for a level to a described late-game sequence (FIBA: 2 in the first half, 3 in the second with at most 2 in the last 2:00, 1 per OT).
ek: FIBA: unused timeouts don't carry; the scoring team can't take one after a goal in the last 2:00 unless play was interrupted.

topics.title: Special situations — BLOB, SLOB, last-second plays

los.do: Choose a baseline or sideline out-of-bounds set for a described need (quick two, a three, a safe inbound) and identify the primary and the safety.
ek: Every inbound set has a scoring option and a safety; the 5-s count starts when the inbounder has the ball.

los.do: Given time on the clock for a last inbound, choose a feasible action (catch-and-shoot, tip, full-court pass, quick hit).
ek: The clock starts on the touch inbounds, not the throw; with fractions of a second only a tip or a quick catch-and-release is realistic.

los.do: Defend a described last-second inbound: choose whether to guard the inbounder, switch everything, or deny the shooter.
ek: Leaving the inbounder adds a defender; switching everything stops screens from freeing the shooter; up 3, take the three away first.

los.do: Given a described sequence, state the shot-clock reset for the level (FIBA 24 / 14; NCAA men 30 / 20 off the rim in the frontcourt).
ek: FIBA: frontcourt throw-in after a stoppage resets to 14 if 13 or fewer remain. NCAA men: ball hits the rim and the offense keeps it in the frontcourt ⇒ 20; in the backcourt ⇒ 30.

los.do: Identify the violation in a described play — 3 s, 5 s closely guarded, 5 s throw-in, 8 s backcourt, backcourt, travel — and its penalty.
ek: FIBA: 3 s in the restricted area; 5 s closely guarded or to release a throw-in; 8 s to cross half-court.

los.do: Given a level and a team-foul count, state the free throws awarded on a non-shooting foul.
ek: NFHS: two shots from the 5th team foul per quarter, reset each quarter. NCAA men: 1-and-1 from the 7th, two from the 10th per half. NCAA women: two from the 5th per quarter. FIBA: two after 4 per quarter; OT fouls count to the 4th quarter.

los.do: State the free throws for a shooting foul (made two, missed two, missed three) and for an unsportsmanlike foul.
ek: Made: count + 1; missed 2-pt: 2; missed 3-pt: 3. FIBA unsportsmanlike: free throws plus a frontcourt throw-in; two unsportsmanlike (or technical) fouls disqualify.

los.do: Judge whether a described late-game foul is a common foul or unsportsmanlike under FIBA criteria.
ek: Unsportsmanlike: no legitimate attempt to play the ball, excessive contact, stopping a fast break, or contact from behind with no defender between the player and the basket.

los.do: Call a described block/charge play using the legal-guarding-position standard.
ek: NCAA (2023-24): the defender must be in legal guarding position before the offensive player's plant foot lands to go airborne.

los.do: Call goaltending or basket interference in a described play and state the result.
ek: Goaltending: touching a shot completely above the ring on its downward flight or after it hits the board. Defense ⇒ points awarded; offense ⇒ no points, throw-in to the opponent.

los.do: Use knowledge of officiating mechanics (crew positions, primary coverage areas) to predict which calls are likely missed and adjust tactics.
ek: Each official covers a primary area; action outside it, or screened by bodies, is called less often.

los.do: Compute a team's possessions from a box score.
ek: Poss ≈ FGA − ORB + TOV + 0.44·FTA; average the two teams' estimates for one game.

los.do: Compute points per possession, offensive and defensive rating (per 100), and net rating from a box score.
ek: ORtg = 100·PTS/Poss; DRtg = 100·Opp PTS/Poss; net = ORtg − DRtg. Pace = possessions per 40 or 48 minutes.

los.do: Explain why per-possession numbers beat per-game numbers when comparing a fast team and a slow team, using a worked comparison.
ek: Points per game mixes pace with efficiency; per-100 isolates efficiency.

los.do: Compute eFG% from FGM, 3PM and FGA, and explain why it exceeds FG% for three-point shooters.
ek: eFG% = (FGM + 0.5·3PM)/FGA: a three counts as 1.5 makes.

los.do: Compute TS% and true shot attempts from PTS, FGA and FTA.
ek: TS% = PTS / (2·(FGA + 0.44·FTA)); 0.44 reflects the mix of 2-shot, 3-shot and and-one trips (0.5 if all were 2-shot) and differs by league.

los.do: Compare two players' efficiency with FG%, eFG% and TS%, and say which measure fits the question.
ek: FG% ignores threes and FTs; eFG% adds threes; TS% adds free throws.

los.do: Compute all four factors for both teams from a box score.
ek: eFG%; TOV% = TOV/(FGA + 0.44·FTA + TOV); ORB% = ORB/(ORB + Opp DRB); FT rate = FT/FGA (bbref) or FTA/FGA (kenpom).

los.do: Given two teams' four factors, identify which factor decided the game and weigh it.
ek: Oliver's approximate weights: shooting 40%, turnovers 25%, rebounding 20%, free throws 15%.

los.do: Translate a four-factors deficit into a coaching emphasis (shot selection, ball security, crashing, attacking the rim).
ek: Each factor maps to a controllable habit; fix the largest weighted gap first.

topics.title: Expected value of shots and decisions

los.do: Compute the expected points of a shot from its make probability and value, and compare shot types (corner three, above-the-break three, mid-range, rim).
ek: EV = p × points: 36% from three ≈ 1.08; 50% at two = 1.00; 40% mid-range = 0.80.
Shooting fouls add value: fold in P(foul) × expected FT points.

los.do: Compute the break-even make percentage at which a three equals a given two, and use it to judge a shot choice.
ek: Break-even p₃ = (2·p₂)/3; a 50% two equals a 33.3% three.

los.do: Include offensive rebounding in a shot's expected value and compare a quick shot with working for a better one.
ek: EV ≈ p·v + (1 − p)·ORB%·PPP_second-chance; passing up a shot costs some turnover risk and clock.

los.do: Judge whether a described stat (a shooter's 3P%, a lineup's net rating, a late-game study) has enough sample to act on.
ek: Three-point percentage and small-lineup ratings are noisy over a few hundred attempts or possessions; late-game samples are tiny and coaches choose when to foul.

los.do: Identify selection bias or role confounding in a described analytic claim (e.g. 'defensive stops are higher when X is on the floor').
ek: Who plays, against whom and when is chosen, not random; on/off numbers carry teammates and opponents with them.

los.do: From a described player profile (shot chart, hand, tendencies), write the defensive key: force direction, closeout type, ball-screen coverage.
ek: A personnel key states what to take away and what to concede, in a few words players can use in the game.

los.do: Classify an opponent's players as shooter, driver, post or non-threat and set help rules from it.
ek: Help off non-shooters, stay home on shooters; label each player so help rules follow.

los.do: Identify an opponent's base offense, main sets and ATO tendencies from described film clips.
ek: Tag first action, entry, and the shot it creates; repeated actions are the scout.

los.do: Identify an opponent's ball-screen coverage and help rules from described clips, and pick the counter you would run.
ek: Read the screener's defender first; the coverage plus the tagger tells you the open pass.

los.do: Self-scout: from your own tagged possessions, find the action with the lowest points per possession and say what to change.
ek: Rank actions by PPP with sample size; small samples flag where to look, not what to conclude.

los.do: Place a described player on the USA Basketball level (Introductory, Foundational, Advanced, Performance) by skill mastery, not age, and name the matching LTAD stage.
ek: Levels are by mastery; LTAD stages run Active Start (0–6), Fundamentals (6–9), Learning to Train (8–12), Training to Train (12–15), Training to Compete (14–17), Training to Win (17+).

los.do: Set the training-to-competition balance and position policy for a level.
ek: Foundational 70:30; Advanced 60:40 shifting to 50:50; Performance 25:75. Foundational: teach position concepts but don't assign positions.

los.do: Sequence team concepts by level: what to teach before 5-on-5, when help-side defense enters, when positions are assigned.
ek: Introductory: team principles only, no 5-on-5 yet, no on-ball defending; help-side comes later; positions may be assigned late in Advanced.

los.do: Convert a principle (e.g. drive-and-kick reads) into a small-sided, competitive drill with live defenders and a scoring rule that rewards the right decision.
ek: Decisions transfer from representative reps: live defense, game spacing, time pressure; scoring rewards the read, not just the make.

los.do: Build a practice plan with progression (1-on-1 → 2-on-2 → 3-on-3 → 5-on-5), time blocks and stated objectives for a given week.
ek: Add players to add reads; every block names the objective it serves.

los.do: Write a short teaching cue for a skill or read and check that it names an observable action.
ek: Cues like B.E.E.F. (balance, elbow, eyes, follow-through) compress a model into words a player can act on mid-rep.

los.do: Design an evaluation of a player's decision-making (tagged reads correct / total) separate from shot-making.
ek: A right read that misses is still a right read; grade decisions and outcomes separately.

los.do: Set season-level team goals from the four factors and track them per game.
ek: Targets for each factor, on both ends, turn analytics into weekly practice priorities.
